# driver

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/driver"
```

Package driver compiles TGo modules and returns their output files.

The driver implements Compile\(directory\). It finds the enclosing Go module, copies its files into a work directory, and prepares selected TGo sources for Go parsing. Go's package loader supplies build selection, syntax, and types.

The driver calls internal/frontend to record postfix operators and introduce success\-only helper calls. Repeated package loading resolves nested calls. It checks final error results, forbidden unsafe operands, and whether the containing function can return each propagated error.

It then passes the typed package and propagation records to internal/lowering. The returned Go replaces helper calls with actual calls, checks, and returns. Physical source paths control file selection even when line directives change diagnostic locations.

The result is a map of module\-relative file names to contents, including source and assets. For example, name\_test.tgo adds name\_tgo\_test.go. The architecture explains the compilation passes and package dependencies.

## func Compile

```go
func Compile(dir string) map[string][]byte
```

Compile translates the module's TGo files and returns file contents by module\-relative path. It keeps other module files in the result and panics on invalid source or compiler failures.
